**13. POWERS, RESPONSIBILITIES AND RELATIONSHIP WITH COUNCIL**

13.1 The Committee is established as a consultative and advisory body of Willoughby City Council
(the Council) and, subject to the Local Government Act 1993 (NSW) and any relevant Council policy,
shall exercise the powers and discharge the responsibilities conferred upon it by these bylaws.

13.2 The Committee shall advise the Council on the planning, development, promotion, and
evaluation of library programs and services for the Willoughby local government area. In
performing this function, the Committee shall have regard to the Council’s adopted library
strategy, the Willoughby Community Strategic Plan, and any other relevant Council policy or
resolution.

13.3 In addition to the powers otherwise conferred by these bylaws, the Committee shall have the
following powers:

(a) to make recommendations to the Council on the development of new library programs and
services, and on the modification or discontinuation of existing programs and services;

(b) to recommend priorities for the allocation of funds within the annual library programs
budget, subject to the final approval of the Council;

(c) to review and comment upon draft policies, procedures, and program plans referred to it by
the Council or by the Library Manager;

(d) to require any sub-committee or working group established under clause 10 to report to it,
and to consider and act upon such reports;

(e) to nominate members to serve on external advisory bodies or community consultative forums
where such representation is sought by the Council; and

(f) to do all things necessary or convenient to be done for or in connection with the exercise of
its functions, except those things which these bylaws or a resolution of the Council expressly
require to be done by the Council itself.

13.4 The powers of the Committee are advisory and recommendatory in nature. Nothing in these
bylaws shall be construed as delegating to the Committee any of the Council’s functions,
powers, or duties under the Local Government Act 1993 (NSW), including but not limited to the

on behalf of the Council. The Committee shall not incur any expenditure on behalf of the Council
except in accordance with a budget approved by the Council or a specific authorisation given by
the Council.

13.5 The Committee shall perform the following responsibilities:

(a) to consider, at least once each financial year, the library programs budget as proposed by
the Library Manager and to provide its recommendations to the Council;

(b) to monitor the delivery of library programs and services against the objectives and
performance indicators set out in the library strategy and in any annual programs plan adopted
by the Council;

(c) to identify emerging community needs and opportunities for library programming, and to
bring these to the attention of the Library Manager and the Council;

(d) to encourage community participation in library programs and to promote the library as a
community resource;

(e) to foster partnerships with local schools, community groups, cultural organisations, and
other bodies for the purpose of enriching the library’s program offering; and

(f) to report annually to the Council on the activities of the Committee, including its
achievements, recommendations, and any matters requiring the attention of the Council.

13.6 The Library Manager, or a nominee of the Library Manager, shall attend meetings of the
Committee in an advisory capacity. The Library Manager shall provide the Committee with such
reports, data, and other information as may reasonably be required for the Committee to perform
its functions. The attendance of the Library Manager shall not count towards the quorum
requirements set out in clause 5.
13.7 The Committee shall keep a register of the interests of its members, which shall be
maintained by the Secretary and made available for inspection by any member of the
public during ordinary business hours at the Willoughby Library administration office.
Each member shall, upon appointment and thereafter annually, disclose in writing any
pecuniary or other interest that may conflict, or appear to conflict, with the proper
performance of the Committee’s functions. A member who has a material interest in a
matter being considered by the Committee shall disclose that interest prior to any
discussion of the matter, shall not take part in the deliberation or vote on the matter,
and shall withdraw from the meeting room while the matter is discussed unless the
Committee, by resolution, determines otherwise. A failure to disclose an interest in
accordance with this clause may be treated by the Committee as a ground for
recommending to the Council that the member be removed from office.

13.8 The Committee shall cause minutes to be kept of each meeting. The minutes shall
record:

(a) the names of the members present and of any apologies tendered and accepted;

(b) the matters considered and the decisions taken, including the terms of each
motion and the names of the mover and seconder;

(c) the result of any vote taken, including the number of votes for and against and the
names of any members abstaining;

(d) any disclosures of interest made under clause 13.7 and the manner in which the
Committee dealt with the disclosure; and

(e) any reports tabled or received, and any correspondence or other documents
circulated in connection with the business of the meeting.

Minutes shall be confirmed at the next ordinary meeting of the Committee and shall be
signed by the Chairperson upon confirmation. Once confirmed, the minutes shall be

13.9 The Committee shall cause proper financial records to be kept in respect of any
funds administered by the Committee and shall provide a financial report to the Council

14. AMENDMENT OF BYLAWS

14.1 These bylaws may be amended by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of
the members present and voting at a meeting of the Committee of which at least
fourteen days’ written notice, specifying the proposed amendment, has been given to
each member.

14.2 An amendment proposed under clause 14.1 shall take effect upon the later of:

(a) the date of the meeting at which the amendment is passed; or

(b) the date, if any, specified in the resolution.

14.3 A copy of any amendment shall be provided to the Council within fourteen days of
the meeting at which it is passed.

15.1 If any provision of these bylaws is held to be invalid, unlawful, or unenforceable,

15.2 The Committee shall not, by reason of any such invalidity, be relieved of any duty

3. PUBLIC FACILITIES

The library operates across two levels with lift access to all public areas.

- Adult fiction and non-fiction collections
- Young adult and junior collections
- Local history and heritage collection
- Children's activity area with play space
- Quiet reading room (Level 2, west wing)

- Baby change table (Level 1, amenities block)
- Water bottle refill station near the main entrance
- Bicycle racks on Victoria Ave footpath

4. ACCESSIBILITY

The library is fully accessible to wheelchair users. The main entrance is at street level with an automatic door. A lift provides access to Level 2. Hearing loop available at the main service desk and in both meeting rooms. Large-print materials collection is located adjacent to the service desk.

Disabled parking: two spaces on Victoria Ave directly outside the library, plus additional spaces in the Chatswood Mall car park.

Meeting rooms may be booked by community groups, not-for-profit organisations, and library program partners. Rooms are available during library opening hours.

- North Shore Room: capacity 10 people, boardroom style, TV screen with HDMI input. Hire fee $35 per hour (community rate).

Priority is given to library programs and events. Bookings may be made up to three months in advance. To reserve a room, contact the library events coordinator at events.library@willoughby.nsw.gov.au or call (02) 9777 7900 during business hours.

Cancellation policy: bookings must be cancelled at least 48 hours before the scheduled start time to avoid a cancellation fee of $25.

Air conditioning servicing is scheduled quarterly. The lift is inspected monthly by the contracted maintenance provider. Fire evacuation drills are held twice per year, most recently on 12 May 2025.

## 8. STAFF ROLES AND SERVICE HOURS

### 8.1 Staffing Structure

The library is staffed by a team of qualified librarians, library technicians, and customer service officers. Staffing levels are maintained to ensure at least two staff members are on duty at all times during opening hours.

| Role | Responsibility | Number of Staff |

### 8.2 Customer Service Policies

The following policies apply to all customer service interactions:

- **Service standard:** All customers are to be greeted within two minutes of approaching the service desk. Staff will wear name badges at all times.
- **Response times for enquiries:** In-person and phone enquiries are answered immediately. Written enquiries (email or letter) are responded to within five business days.
- **Privacy:** Customer borrowing records are confidential. Staff may not disclose borrowing history to any third party, including family members, without a court order.
- **Complaints procedure:** Customers who wish to make a complaint may do so in person, by phone, or in writing. Complaints are acknowledged within three business days and resolved within 15 business days. Escalation to the Library Manager occurs if resolution is not achieved within that timeframe.
- **Mobile phone use:** Customers are asked to take phone calls outside the quiet study areas. Phone use is permitted throughout the rest of the library.
- **Food and drink:** Covered drinks are permitted throughout the library. Food is only permitted in the foyer area and meeting rooms when booked.
- **Unattended children:** Children under eight years of age must be accompanied by a responsible adult or carer aged 16 years or older at all times. Staff reserve the right to contact emergency services if a child appears to be unattended.
- **Photography:** Photography and filming for personal use is permitted. Commercial photography or filming requires prior written approval from the Library Manager.

3.2 *Action Item 16 (May meeting):* Priya Sharma reported that the draft volunteer handbook has been updated to reflect the new privacy policy and is now available in the shared drive. The handbook will be circulated to all volunteers before the end of term. Item closed.

3.3 *Action Item 18 (May meeting):* Liam O'Donnell advised that the proposed partnership with the Willoughby Business Chamber for the Spring Festival has not yet received a response. He will follow up by the end of June. Item remains open.

**4. Reports**

**4.1 Chair's Report**

The Chair thanked members for their contributions over the 2024–2025 term. She noted that the Committee had delivered two successful school holiday programs, the Summer Reading Challenge 2024, and the inaugural Willoughby Writers' Festival in March 2025, which attracted over 300 attendees.

The Chair reported that the Library's programming budget for the 2025–2026 financial year has been confirmed, with an increase of 3.5% over the current year. This includes dedicated funding for a new adult literacy conversation group, to be piloted in Term 3.

The Chair also noted that the Library will be hosting a visit from the State Library of NSW's outreach team in August 2025 to deliver a staff development session on inclusive programming. Committee members are welcome to attend.

**4.2 Treasurer's Report**

Grace Kim presented the financial report for the year ending 30 June 2025. A full statement of income and expenditure was circulated. Key points:

- Closing balance in the programming account as at 31 May 2025: $14,203.15
- Estimated closing balance at 30 June 2025: $13,480.00 (after payment of outstanding invoices)
- All invoices for the 2024–2025 financial year have been received; the final two payments are scheduled for late June
- The June school holiday program (30 June – 11 July 2025) is fully booked, with projected income of $1,850.00 from ticket sales
- A surplus of $640.00 was returned from the Autumn Festival stall held in April

Maya Chen's term end date is 2026-06-30. Record status: current.

The Committee noted the financial report.

**Resolved** that the financial report for the year ending 30 June 2025 be accepted and that the final accounts be presented for audit in July.

Moved: Grace Kim. Seconded: Sarah Nguyen. Carried.

**4.3 Events Lead Report**

Liam O'Donnell provided a summary of the June school holiday program (30 June – 11 July 2025):

- All 14 sessions are fully booked, with a combined waitlist of 43 children
- The most popular session is "Brick Builders: Architecture Challenge" on 7 July, with a waitlist of 18
- The "Junior Book Club: Graphic Novels" session on 3 July has been moved to the larger meeting room to accommodate demand
- Feedback from the May program was positive, with an average rating of 4.6 out of 5

Liam noted that planning for the September school holidays (29 September – 10 October 2025) will commence in July. He proposed a repeat of the Brick Builders session and a new "Coding for Beginners" workshop for children aged 8–12. The Committee supported these proposals.

**4.4 Volunteer Coordinator Report**

Priya Sharma reported that there are currently 26 active volunteers. Three new volunteers completed induction training on 2 June 2025, and one volunteer has stepped down due to relocation.

Priya noted that volunteer rostering for the Summer Reading Challenge 2025–2026 will commence in August 2025. She will circulate a request for expressions of interest to all volunteers in the first week of July.
**5.1 Community Engagement Grant**
Grace Kim, as the Committee’s Grants Liaison, reported that the application for the Willoughby City Council Community Engagement Grant (up to $3,000) was submitted on 10 February 2025. The application sought funding for the proposed “Stories in the Park” outreach program, which would deliver fortnightly storytime sessions at three local parks during the spring school term.

Grace advised that Council had requested further information regarding the program’s target audience and proposed evaluation measures. She had provided this information by email on 12 February 2025. Council has indicated that a decision is expected by mid-March 2025.

The Committee discussed the program’s alignment with the Library’s strategic priority of increasing outreach to families in the eastern part of the Willoughby local government area. It was noted that the program would require two staff members per session and a minimum of four volunteers to assist with setup and activity supervision.

**Resolved** that the Committee endorse the “Stories in the Park” program proposal as submitted, and that Grace Kim be authorised to accept the grant on behalf of the Committee should the application be successful.

Moved: Grace Kim. Seconded: Sarah Nguyen. Carried.

**5.2 Volunteer Training Workshop**
Priya Sharma reported that the proposed volunteer training workshop, “Supporting Neurodiverse Patrons,” had been scheduled for Saturday 26 July 2025, from 10:00 to 13:00, in the Library’s Learning Centre. The workshop will be facilitated by an external trainer from North Shore Community Services, at a cost of $350.00.

Priya noted that the workshop was developed in response to feedback from volunteers who expressed a need for more confidence in assisting patrons with autism and ADHD. The workshop will cover communication strategies, sensory considerations, and de-escalation techniques.

The Committee discussed the proposed cost and agreed that it represents good value given the trainer’s expertise. Priya will circulate a flyer to all volunteers by 30 June 2025 and will open registrations on a first-come, first-served basis. A maximum of 20 participants will be accepted.

**Resolved** that the Committee approve the expenditure of up to $350.00 for the volunteer training workshop.

Moved: Priya Sharma. Seconded: Liam O’Donnell. Carried.

Liam O’Donnell provided an update on the Tech Talks Series, which will run on the first Thursday of each month from August to November 2025. The series is aimed at adults and will cover the following topics:

- August: “Getting Started with Your Smartphone”
- September: “Staying Safe Online”
- October: “Using MyGov and Digital Identity”

Liam noted that the projector in the Learning Centre has been booked for all four sessions, and that the Library’s IT Support Officer has agreed to be on standby for the first session in each room.

Liam will also prepare a short video teaser, to be posted on the Library’s social media channels in the last week of July.

4.2 The Chair shall be elected by the members at the first ordinary meeting of each program year and shall hold office for that program year. The Chair shall:

(a) preside at all meetings of the Committee;

(b) prepare the agenda in consultation with the Secretary and the Library Manager;

(c) represent the Committee in communications with the Library Manager and Council officers.

4.3 The Deputy Chair shall be elected at the same meeting as the Chair and shall preside in the Chair's absence. If the Chair and Deputy Chair are both absent, the members present shall elect a Chair for that meeting.

4.4 The Secretary shall be appointed by the Chair, with the agreement of the Committee, and need not be a member. The Secretary shall:

(a) issue notices of meetings;

(b) record minutes of each meeting;

(c) maintain the Committee's records, including attendance registers and action lists;

(d) manage correspondence on behalf of the Committee.

4.5 The Library Manager, or their nominee, shall not be eligible for election as Chair.

---

**5. CONFLICT OF INTEREST**

5.1 A member who has a material personal interest in a matter being considered by the Committee shall:

(a) disclose the nature of the interest to the Committee before the matter is discussed;

(b) not be present during the discussion or vote on that matter, unless the Committee resolves otherwise.

5.2 Disclosures shall be recorded in the minutes.

---

**6. MEETINGS**

6.1 The Committee shall meet monthly, ordinarily on the second Tuesday of each month at 10:00, at the Library or at another location determined by the Chair. Willoughby Library Programming Committee meeting_frequency monthly. Record status: current.

6.2 Ordinary meeting dates for the program year shall be scheduled at the first ordinary meeting of that year and circulated to all members.

6.3 Special meetings may be called by the Chair or by the Library Manager, upon at least forty-eight (48) hours' notice to each member, specifying the business to be considered. Only that business may be transacted at a special meeting.

6.4 The Chair may cancel an ordinary meeting if fewer than three (3) items of business are available for the agenda, or if a public holiday falls on the scheduled date. Notice of cancellation shall be given to all members at least five (5) days before the scheduled date.

6.5 Meetings may be held in person, by telephone, or by video conference, provided that all members participating can communicate with each other simultaneously.

---

**7. QUORUM AND VOTING**

7.1 A quorum shall be a majority of the current members of the Committee.

7.2 No business shall be transacted at a meeting unless a quorum is present at the commencement of the meeting and at the time the business is considered.

7.3 If a quorum is not present within fifteen (15) minutes of the scheduled start time, the meeting shall stand adjourned to the same time and place in the following week. If a quorum is not present at the adjourned meeting, the members present may proceed with the agenda, provided that no resolution involving expenditure of funds shall be passed.

7.4 Each member present shall have one (1) vote. The Chair shall have a deliberative vote and, in the event of an equality of votes, a second or casting vote.

7.5 Except as otherwise provided in these bylaws, questions arising at a meeting shall be decided by a majority of votes of members present and voting.

7.6 A member may not vote by proxy.

---

**8. AGENDA AND MINUTES**

8.1 The Secretary shall circulate the agenda and supporting papers to members no fewer than five (5) days before each ordinary meeting.

8.2 Items for the agenda shall be submitted to the Secretary no fewer than seven (7) days before the meeting.

If a member withdraws from a meeting such that a quorum ceases to be present, no further business shall be transacted until the quorum is restored.

7.12 For the purpose of determining a quorum, members participating by telephone or video conference shall be counted as present, provided that they can be identified and can hear and be heard by all other participants.

---

**8. AGENDA AND MINUTES** *(continued)*

8.4 The minutes of each meeting shall be confirmed at the next ordinary meeting, or at a special meeting called for that purpose, before being entered into the official record. Once confirmed, the minutes shall be signed by the Chair and dated.

8.5 The Secretary shall keep a register of attendance and shall record, for each meeting, the names of members present, the names of members absent, and whether a quorum was formed.

8.6 Minutes shall be made available to members within ten (10) days after each meeting and shall be available for inspection by any member of the public upon request to the Library.

---

**9. OFFICERS**

9.1 The officers of the Committee shall be the Chair, the Deputy Chair, the Secretary, and the Treasurer. All officers shall be elected by the Committee from among its members at the first ordinary meeting following the annual general meeting of the Library.

9.2 The Chair shall preside at all meetings of the Committee, shall have a deliberative vote, and shall exercise a casting vote in the event of an equality of votes, as provided in clause 7.4.

9.4 The Secretary shall:
(a) give notice of meetings and circulate agendas and supporting papers as required by these bylaws;
(b) keep the minutes and the register of attendance;
(c) maintain the Committee's official records and correspondence; and
(d) perform such other duties as the Committee may direct.

9.5 The Treasurer shall:
(a) oversee the Committee's funds and accounts;
(b) present a financial report at each ordinary meeting;
(c) prepare the annual budget for the Committee's approval; and
(d) arrange for the custody of the Committee's financial records.

9.6 An officer shall hold office for a term of one (1) year and may be re-elected for further terms.

9.7 A vacancy in any office shall be filled at the next ordinary meeting, or at a special meeting called for that purpose.

---

**10. COMMITTEES AND WORKING GROUPS**

10.1 The Committee may establish sub-committees or working groups for specific purposes, and may determine their membership, terms of reference, and duration.

The Willoughby Library Programming Committee's quorum is 5 members. Record status: current.

10.2 A sub-committee may include persons who are not members of the Committee, provided that the Chair of any sub-committee shall be a member of the Committee.

---

**11. FINANCIAL PROVISIONS**

11.1 The Committee shall not incur expenditure exceeding one thousand dollars ($1,000) without the prior approval of the Committee at a meeting where a quorum is present.

11.2 The Treasurer shall keep proper books of account and shall present a statement of income and expenditure at each ordinary meeting.

---

**12. AMENDMENT OF BYLAWS**

12.2 No amendment shall take effect until it has been recorded in the minutes and circulated to all members.

---

**13. DISSOLUTION**

13.2 Upon dissolution, any remaining funds or assets of the Committee shall be transferred to the Willoughby City Library for the purchase of library materials, unless the Committee resolves otherwise at the time of dissolution.

---

**14. ADOPTION AND AMENDMENT RECORD**

14.1 These bylaws were adopted by the Committee on 1 July 2019.

14.2 The bylaws were amended on 15 November 2023. The amendments take effect on 1 January 2024 and are reflected in the current version of these bylaws.

**9. OFFICERS** (continued)

9.8 The Chair shall preside at all meetings of the Committee and shall have a casting vote in
addition to an ordinary vote. In the absence of the Chair, the Vice-Chair shall preside and shall
exercise the same powers, including the casting vote.

9.9 The Secretary shall be responsible for the custody of the Committee's records, including the
minutes of meetings, the register of members, and the current version of these bylaws. The Secretary
shall give notice of all meetings in accordance with section 6.3 and shall conduct the
correspondence of the Committee.

9.10 The Vice-Chair shall, in the absence of the Chair, perform the duties of the Chair. The
Vice-Chair may also be delegated specific duties by the Chair or by the Committee.

9.11 No officer shall receive remuneration for their service, but the Committee may reimburse
reasonable out-of-pocket expenses incurred in the performance of official duties, upon production of
receipts.

9.12 An officer shall be elected by a simple majority of members present and voting at an ordinary
meeting. Nominations shall be received in writing by the Secretary no later than seven (7) days
before the meeting. A member may nominate themself. If no nomination is received for an office, the
Chair shall call for nominations from the floor at the meeting.

9.13 Elections shall be conducted by a show of hands, unless a ballot is requested by at least two
(2) members present. The result of each election shall be recorded in the minutes.

9.14 The term of office shall commence at the close of the meeting at which the election is held and
shall expire at the close of the ordinary meeting in the corresponding month of the following year,
or at the close of the annual general meeting, whichever occurs first.

9.15 For the purposes of these bylaws, the offices of Chair, Vice-Chair, Secretary, and Treasurer
constitute the Executive of the Committee. The Executive may meet between ordinary meetings to
attend to urgent matters, provided that any decision made by the Executive shall be reported to the
Committee at its next ordinary meeting and shall not be implemented until ratified, unless the
Committee has previously authorised the Executive to act.

**10. COMMITTEES AND WORKING GROUPS** (continued)

10.3 Unless otherwise specified in the terms of reference, each sub-committee shall report to the
Committee at each ordinary meeting and shall provide a written summary of its activities,
including any recommendations for action.

10.4 A sub-committee shall dissolve upon completion of its purpose, or upon a resolution of the
Committee, or at the end of the term specified in its terms of reference, whichever occurs first.

**11. FINANCIAL PROVISIONS** (continued)

11.3 The Committee shall review its financial position at the first ordinary meeting of each
financial year and shall consider whether any adjustments to the annual budget are required.

11.4 All cheques and electronic payments shall be authorised by any two (2) of the following
officers: Chair, Treasurer, or Secretary.

**12. AMENDMENT OF BYLAWS** (continued)

12.3 A proposed amendment may be submitted by any member in writing at an ordinary meeting, or by
notice to the Secretary at least fourteen (14) days before an ordinary meeting. The proposal shall
be read at the meeting and shall be considered for adoption at the next ordinary meeting, unless
the Committee resolves to consider it earlier.

**14. ADOPTION AND AMENDMENT RECORD** (continued)

14.3 A consolidated version of these bylaws, incorporating all amendments, shall be maintained by
the Secretary and shall be made available to members upon request.

**13. POWERS, RESPONSIBILITIES AND RELATIONSHIP WITH COUNCIL**

13.1 The Committee is established as a consultative and advisory body of Willoughby City Council
(the Council) and, subject to the Local Government Act 1993 (NSW) and any relevant Council policy,
shall exercise the powers and discharge the responsibilities conferred upon it by these bylaws.

13.2 The Committee shall advise the Council on the planning, development, promotion, and
evaluation of library programs and services for the Willoughby local government area. In
performing this function, the Committee shall have regard to the Council’s adopted library
strategy, the Willoughby Community Strategic Plan, and any other relevant Council policy or
resolution.

13.3 In addition to the powers otherwise conferred by these bylaws, the Committee shall have the
following powers:

(a) to make recommendations to the Council on the development of new library programs and
services, and on the modification or discontinuation of existing programs and services;

(b) to recommend priorities for the allocation of funds within the annual library programs
budget, subject to the final approval of the Council;

(c) to review and comment upon draft policies, procedures, and program plans referred to it by
the Council or by the Library Manager;

(d) to require any sub-committee or working group established under clause 10 to report to it,
and to consider and act upon such reports;

(e) to nominate members to serve on external advisory bodies or community consultative forums
where such representation is sought by the Council; and

(f) to do all things necessary or convenient to be done for or in connection with the exercise of
its functions, except those things which these bylaws or a resolution of the Council expressly
require to be done by the Council itself.

13.4 The powers of the Committee are advisory and recommendatory in nature. Nothing in these
bylaws shall be construed as delegating to the Committee any of the Council’s functions,
powers, or duties under the Local Government Act 1993 (NSW), including but not limited to the
power to levy rates, to borrow money, to acquire or dispose of land, or to enter into contracts
on behalf of the Council. The Committee shall not incur any expenditure on behalf of the Council
except in accordance with a budget approved by the Council or a specific authorisation given by
the Council.

13.5 The Committee shall perform the following responsibilities:

(a) to consider, at least once each financial year, the library programs budget as proposed by
the Library Manager and to provide its recommendations to the Council;

(b) to monitor the delivery of library programs and services against the objectives and
performance indicators set out in the library strategy and in any annual programs plan adopted
by the Council;

(c) to identify emerging community needs and opportunities for library programming, and to
bring these to the attention of the Library Manager and the Council;

(d) to encourage community participation in library programs and to promote the library as a
community resource;

(e) to foster partnerships with local schools, community groups, cultural organisations, and
other bodies for the purpose of enriching the library’s program offering; and

(f) to report annually to the Council on the activities of the Committee, including its
achievements, recommendations, and any matters requiring the attention of the Council.

13.6 The Library Manager, or a nominee of the Library Manager, shall attend meetings of the
Committee in an advisory capacity. The Library Manager shall provide the Committee with such
reports, data, and other information as may reasonably be required for the Committee to perform
its functions. The attendance of the Library Manager shall not count towards the quorum
requirements set out in clause 5.

13.7 The Committee shall keep a register of the interests of its members, which shall be
maintained by the Secretary and made available for inspection by any member of the
public during ordinary business hours at the Willoughby Library administration office.
Each member shall, upon appointment and thereafter annually, disclose in writing any
pecuniary or other interest that may conflict, or appear to conflict, with the proper
performance of the Committee’s functions. A member who has a material interest in a
matter being considered by the Committee shall disclose that interest prior to any
discussion of the matter, shall not take part in the deliberation or vote on the matter,
and shall withdraw from the meeting room while the matter is discussed unless the
Committee, by resolution, determines otherwise. A failure to disclose an interest in
accordance with this clause may be treated by the Committee as a ground for
recommending to the Council that the member be removed from office.

13.8 The Committee shall cause minutes to be kept of each meeting. The minutes shall
record:

(a) the names of the members present and of any apologies tendered and accepted;

(b) the matters considered and the decisions taken, including the terms of each
motion and the names of the mover and seconder;

(c) the result of any vote taken, including the number of votes for and against and the
names of any members abstaining;

(d) any disclosures of interest made under clause 13.7 and the manner in which the
Committee dealt with the disclosure; and

(e) any reports tabled or received, and any correspondence or other documents
circulated in connection with the business of the meeting.

Minutes shall be confirmed at the next ordinary meeting of the Committee and shall be
signed by the Chairperson upon confirmation. Once confirmed, the minutes shall be
retained by the Secretary in the Committee’s records for a period of not less than seven
years.

13.9 The Committee shall cause proper financial records to be kept in respect of any
funds administered by the Committee and shall provide a financial report to the Council
at least once each financial year, or more frequently if the Council so requires. The
financial report shall include a statement of income and expenditure, a statement of any
unexpended funds, and such other information as the Council may reasonably require.

14. AMENDMENT OF BYLAWS

14.1 These bylaws may be amended by a resolution passed by a two-thirds majority of
the members present and voting at a meeting of the Committee of which at least
fourteen days’ written notice, specifying the proposed amendment, has been given to
each member.

14.2 An amendment proposed under clause 14.1 shall take effect upon the later of:

(a) the date of the meeting at which the amendment is passed; or

(b) the date, if any, specified in the resolution.

14.3 A copy of any amendment shall be provided to the Council within fourteen days of
the meeting at which it is passed.

15. SEVERABILITY

15.1 If any provision of these bylaws is held to be invalid, unlawful, or unenforceable,
whether in whole or in part, the remaining provisions shall continue in full force and
effect.

15.2 The Committee shall not, by reason of any such invalidity, be relieved of any duty
or obligation imposed by these bylaws to the extent that the duty or obligation is not
itself affected.

16. COMMENCEMENT AND REPEAL

16.1 These bylaws, as amended, take effect on 1 January 2024.

16.2 The bylaws adopted on 1 July 2019, and any amendments made prior to the date
of effect of these bylaws, are repealed and replaced by these bylaws as amended.

16.3 For the avoidance of doubt, any action taken or decision made by the Committee
under the repealed bylaws before the date of effect of these amended bylaws shall not
be invalid by reason only of the repeal.

Sunday: 1:00 pm – 5:00 pm

Public holidays: Closed on all gazetted public holidays. The library closes early (5:00 pm) on Christmas Eve and New Year's Eve.

3. PUBLIC FACILITIES

The library operates across two levels with lift access to all public areas.

- Adult fiction and non-fiction collections
- Young adult and junior collections
- Local history and heritage collection
- Children's activity area with play space
- Quiet reading room (Level 2, west wing)

- Water bottle refill station near the main entrance
- Bicycle racks on Victoria Ave footpath

The library is fully accessible to wheelchair users. The main entrance is at street level with an automatic door. A lift provides access to Level 2. Hearing loop available at the main service desk and in both meeting rooms. Large-print materials collection is located adjacent to the service desk.

Disabled parking: two spaces on Victoria Ave directly outside the library, plus additional spaces in the Chatswood Mall car park.

## 8. STAFF ROLES AND SERVICE HOURS

### 8.1 Staffing Structure

The library is staffed by a team of qualified librarians, library technicians, and customer service officers. Staffing levels are maintained to ensure at least two staff members are on duty at all times during opening hours.

| Role | Responsibility | Number of Staff |
|------|----------------|-----------------|

| Library Technicians | Shelving, processing, IT support | 2 |
| Casual Relief Staff | Covering leave and peak periods | 3 |

### 8.2 Customer Service Policies

The following policies apply to all customer service interactions:

- **Service standard:** All customers are to be greeted within two minutes of approaching the service desk. Staff will wear name badges at all times.
- **Response times for enquiries:** In-person and phone enquiries are answered immediately. Written enquiries (email or letter) are responded to within five business days.
- **Privacy:** Customer borrowing records are confidential. Staff may not disclose borrowing history to any third party, including family members, without a court order.
- **Complaints procedure:** Customers who wish to make a complaint may do so in person, by phone, or in writing. Complaints are acknowledged within three business days and resolved within 15 business days. Escalation to the Library Manager occurs if resolution is not achieved within that timeframe.
- **Mobile phone use:** Customers are asked to take phone calls outside the quiet study areas. Phone use is permitted throughout the rest of the library.
- **Food and drink:** Covered drinks are permitted throughout the library. Food is only permitted in the foyer area and meeting rooms when booked.
- **Unattended children:** Children under eight years of age must be accompanied by a responsible adult or carer aged 16 years or older at all times. Staff reserve the right to contact emergency services if a child appears to be unattended.
- **Photography:** Photography and filming for personal use is permitted. Commercial photography or filming requires prior written approval from the Library Manager.

Grace advised that Council had requested further information regarding the program’s target audience and proposed evaluation measures. She had provided this information by email on 12 February 2025. Council has indicated that a decision is expected by mid-March 2025.

The Committee discussed the program’s alignment with the Library’s strategic priority of increasing outreach to families in the eastern part of the Willoughby local government area. Priya noted that the workshop was developed in response to feedback from volunteers who expressed a need for more confidence in assisting patrons with autism and ADHD. The workshop will cover communication strategies, sensory considerations, and de-escalation techniques.
